event_register.Event Description: Contractor formally requests first delivery of reinforcement steel from Employer.
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: First formal request establishes baseline obligation under SC 4.20. No notice period required as initial requisition.

event_register.Event Description: Contractor revises first delivery quantities due to site constraints.
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: Proactive mitigation adjusting order to match site conditions. Good faith effort demonstrated.

event_register.Event Description: Contractor requests second reinforcement steel delivery.
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: Second formal requisition. First order still incomplete. Cumulative failure pattern established.

event_register.Event Description: Contractor requests third reinforcement steel delivery.
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: Third requisition. First and second orders remain incomplete.

event_register.Event Description: Contractor notifies Employer of steel supply delay and reserves EOT and cost rights. Event02
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: CRITICAL: First formal delay notice under SC 20.1. Issued same day as awareness. Reserves EOT and cost.

event_register.Event Description: Contractor warns steel nearly exhausted and structural works may suspend. Event02
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: Second delay notice. Escalates to warning of imminent suspension. Within 28 days.

event_register.Event Description: Contractor notifies depletion and non-delivery, claims EOT entitlement. Event02
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: Third cumulative notice. Claims EOT. Notes 300 tons self-supplied as mitigation. Within 28 days.

event_register.Event Description: Contractor records late supply of Order 2, requests payment for self-procured steel.
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: Fourth notice. Commercial claim for self-procured steel. Within 28 days. Strong claim.

event_register.Event Description: Contractor notifies Order 2 partly delivered and Order 3 outstanding.
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: Fifth notice. Documents partial delivery. Notes 420+ tons self-supplied.

event_register.Event Description: Contractor records cumulative owner steel delay and mitigation, reserves all entitlements.
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: SIXTH COMPREHENSIVE NOTICE. Synthesizes all prior notices. Claims EOT, costs, all entitlements.

event_register.Event Description: New IFC Issued
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: Revised structure drawing

event_register.Event Description: Complete IFC received as requested from cotractor-SAMCO
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: Issued IFC caused a rework in approved structural shopdrawings in B), B01, B02, B03, B04

event_register.Event Description: Contractor clarifies SAMCO responsibility excludes MEP works by employer-appointed subcontractors.
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: First formal boundary-setting letter. Establishes MEP is outside civil scope.

event_register.Event Description: Engineer rejects Contractor's refusal of VI-0003, demands immediate execution.
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: Engineer issues binding variation. Does not address scope objection. Triggers SC 20.1 obligation.

event_register.Event Description: Contractor rejects execution of MEP works under VI-0003 as outside scope.
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: First formal rejection of VI-0003. Maintains MEP outside scope. Within 28 days.

event_register.Event Description: Contractor formally rejects assignment of MEP works, demands MEP contractor appointment.
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: Second formal rejection. Escalates to general MEP scope principle. Records non-responsibility.

event_register.Event Description: Engineer rejects refusal of VI Ref. 4 (GWT flanges), affirms variation as binding.
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: Engineer reiterates VI is binding. Does not address scope boundary dispute.

event_register.Event Description: Contractor reiterates flanges are MEP/mechanical and outside civil scope.
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: Third rejection. Focus on GWT flanges. Reinforces consistent position across VIs.

event_register.Event Description: Engineer confirms first-fix MEP works are required as variation, no suspension permitted.
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: Engineer interprets contract to require MEP first-fix. Threats damages. Does not resolve scope dispute.

event_register.Event Description: Contractor notifies critical sewage pipeline conflict through tank base slab on critical path.
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: CRITICAL: Identifies MEP interface on critical path. Offers mitigation subject to formal VO and payment. Within 28 days.

event_register.Event Description: Engineer confirms VIs already issued, demands execution and proposal submission.
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: Engineer acknowledges existing VIs. Demands execution. Does not address conditional acceptance.

event_register.Event Description: Contractor accepts first-fix MEP only subject to formal VO, BOQ sharing, and proposal approval.
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: CONDITIONAL ACCEPTANCE: Shifts from rejection to conditional acceptance under SC 13.3. Requires VO, BOQ, approval. Within 28 days.

event_register.Event Description: Contractor notifies RFI delays (RFIs 3,4,5,6) halting tank, sump, electrical, stair activities.
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: Second notice. Specific RFIs identified. Direct causal link documented. EOT and cost reserved.

event_register.Event Description: Contractor issues comprehensive early warning on site progress constraints including RFI 17.
event_register.Demonstration of Compliance with Notice: FIFTH NOTICE: Synthesizes RFI delays with design and material constraints. Explicitly references SC 20.1.

rows.Clause / Topic: Employer free-issue reinforcement steel delay - primary TIA clause
rows.Location: Clause 4.20 / Appendix advance payment steel supply / Clause 8.4 / Clause 20.1
rows.Plain English Meaning: Employer-supplied or client supplied reinforcement steel is tied to the approved programme and advance-payment arrangement. Late, short, or unusable free-issue steel can support a Delay TIA only when the Contractor proves timely requisition, readiness to use the steel, and critical path impact.
rows.Research the Lines: Priority keywords: steel, reinforcement, RFT, free issue, employer supplied, client supplied, material shortage, approved programme, requisition, delivery notes, stock records, activity impacts, critical path, TIA, EOT. This should rank first for steel shortage events. The Contractor position is strongest where the affected activity was ready, predecessors were complete, and the delay window is measured from stock-out/need date to usable recovery.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Shared - Contractor has leverage on time if records prove readiness and criticality; Employer has leverage if requisitions, readiness, or critical path are weak.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Immediate notice under Clause 20.1 and monthly claim account required. State activity ID, required steel date, requested quantity, delivered quantity, shortage, affected programme update, and intended TIA fragnet.
rows.Money Impact: Potential prolongation, disruption, and steel/concrete price adjustment only if non-Contractor delay and no uncompensable concurrency are proven.
rows.Schedule Impact: Strong EOT candidate if the stock-out delays a critical or longest-path activity, consumes float, or delays a contractual milestone after proper TIA insertion.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Approved baseline/update programme; steel requisitions; delivery notes; stock ledger; material inspection records; activity readiness proof; predecessor completion; photos; daily reports; CPM/TIA fragnet; concurrency review; notice and monthly claim updates.

rows.Plain English Meaning: The 25 percent advance includes a steel-supply component, with 70 percent as steel supplied by the Employer according to the approved programme.
rows.Research the Lines: This links free-issue steel to payment and programme administration. It does not by itself prove delay; it proves the source of supply and makes approved programme dates, requisitions, and delivery records central evidence.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify immediately when steel supply under the advance mechanism is late, short, or not usable against approved programme needs.
rows.Money Impact: Affects advance/payment reconciliation and may support prolongation or escalation only when delay responsibility is established.
rows.Schedule Impact: Supports causation for free-issue steel delay if the affected activity was ready and impacted the critical path.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Approved programme; advance-payment terms; steel delivery schedule; requisitions; receipts; delivery notes; shortage calculations; balance curve; correspondence requesting recovery commitments.

rows.Clause / Topic: Extension of Time entitlement and TIA proof
rows.Plain English Meaning: EOT is available only for qualifying Employer/Engineer risk events that delay completion or a contractual milestone and are claimed under the notice procedure.
rows.Research the Lines: Use this row for all Delay TIA conclusions. A valid event needs cause, effect, critical path/float impact, contemporaneous notice, and an update-impact/TIA calculation. Simple addition of delay days is not enough.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Shared - Contractor if critical path proof and notice are strong; Employer if delay is non-critical, concurrent, or unsupported.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Strict Clause 20.1 notice, particulars, updates, and monthly claim account. Missing or late notices create high time-bar risk.
rows.Money Impact: EOT protects from delay damages. Prolongation cost requires separate entitlement, causation, and concurrency proof.
rows.Schedule Impact: Primary schedule entitlement route for steel, RFI, IFC, access, variation, and suspension events.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Delay event register; notice register; impacted update; baseline/update schedules; fragnet logic; narrative; float path comparison; milestone impact; concurrency matrix; mitigation records.

rows.Clause / Topic: Clause 20.1 claim notice and time bar control
rows.Plain English Meaning: Failure to submit timely notice, particulars, and monthly claim updates can waive or severely weaken time and money claims.
rows.Research the Lines: This is the highest-risk defence against every otherwise valid claim. The Delay TIA engine should treat notice compliance as a gating issue, not an administrative afterthought.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Employer unless Contractor has complete notice trail
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Immediate protective notice; detailed particulars when available; repeat in monthly claim/variation account until resolved.
rows.Money Impact: Missed notice can defeat prolongation cost, disruption cost, variation recovery, and interest arguments.
rows.Schedule Impact: Missed notice can defeat or weaken EOT even where the technical schedule impact exists.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Notice letters; submission receipts; Engineer/Employer acknowledgements; monthly claim account; updated particulars; claim register; evidence index; responsible-party chronology.

rows.Clause / Topic: Delayed drawings, IFC revisions and Engineer instructions
rows.Plain English Meaning: Late drawings, delayed instructions, design revisions, or IFC conflicts may be Employer/Engineer risk when they stop approvals, procurement, inspection, or construction activities.
rows.Research the Lines: Use this for IFC conflict, revised structural drawings, missing information, delayed approvals, and RFI response delay. Entitlement depends on request date, required-by date, late response date, actual workface impact, and critical path effect.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify once information is late or revision impact is known; identify affected activities and required response date.
rows.Money Impact: Potential prolongation or variation cost if the revision changes scope or causes non-concurrent delay.
rows.Schedule Impact: Potential EOT if late information delays critical design approval, procurement, inspection, or construction sequence.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: RFI/submittal logs; drawing register; transmittals; revision clouds; response dates; approval workflow; impacted activities; predecessor/successor logic; TIA fragnet; notice letters.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Late responses to RFIs, shop drawings, material approvals, or technical submittals can become a delay event where the response was required before work could proceed.
rows.Research the Lines: The key is not merely that an RFI was late; prove the answer was needed for a specific activity and that no reasonable alternate workfront avoided the impact.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Submit notice when response exceeds contractual/reasonable review period and affects planned work.
rows.Money Impact: Potential cost only if delay is Employer/Engineer risk and not concurrent with Contractor delay.
rows.Schedule Impact: Potential EOT where delayed response blocks critical or near-critical successor work.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: RFI register; submittal register; submission/reply dates; required-by date; affected activity ID; blocked workfront records; consultant comments; programme update; mitigation attempts.

rows.Clause / Topic: Programme requirements and critical path proof
rows.Plain English Meaning: The programme must be a proper CPM/P6 programme with logic, resources/cost/cash-flow where required, and regular updates. Delay claims depend on accepted programme logic.
rows.Research the Lines: The Delay TIA is only as strong as the schedule data. Float, longest path, predecessors, successors, calendars, progress status, and data date must be traceable.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Employer if programme is missing, unapproved, or logic is weak; Contractor if statused updates are complete.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Submit/revise programmes and narratives on time; include delay impacts in monthly reporting and claim accounts.
rows.Money Impact: Weak programme proof weakens prolongation and disruption claims.
rows.Schedule Impact: Critical path and EOT proof depends on accepted/current logic and statused update windows.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Baseline programme; update schedules; XER/PDF exports; calendars; logic report; longest-path report; float report; progress narrative; recovery plans; TIA insertion files.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Concurrent Employer and Contractor delays may allow time relief but can block or reduce money recovery for the concurrent period.
rows.Research the Lines: The concurrency matrix must split Employer delay, Contractor delay, neutral delay, and overlapping windows. Do not double count days. Separate entitlement to time from entitlement to cost.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Employer on money; Contractor may retain time protection if critical Employer delay is proven.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notice still required for each Employer-risk event and each updated impact period.
rows.Money Impact: No or reduced prolongation cost during true concurrency unless contract/legal position supports apportionment.
rows.Schedule Impact: Possible EOT for net critical delay, subject to causation and notice.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Concurrency matrix; event windows; responsible party coding; critical path comparison; float consumption; contractor delay register; mitigation records; narrative explaining net impact.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Project is the Big Project civil works between Roya as Employer and Samco as Contractor, effective 30-Apr-2025.
rows.Beneath the Lines: All later letters should be read against this baseline: parties, project, price, time, and risk allocation are fixed from this date.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Use exact contract references in all notices.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Keep contract date, parties, amount, and commencement records in every claim file.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Contract amount is EGP 367,286,025 including social insurance, duties, and taxes except VAT.
rows.Beneath the Lines: The price is intended to be comprehensive. The Contractor must prove why any extra is outside the agreed scope or qualifies under variation/adjustment clauses.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Any extra must follow Variation or Claim procedure.
rows.Money Impact: High barrier to extra payment unless clear instruction/change exists.
rows.Schedule Impact: No direct time right unless linked to variation or delay event.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: For each extra cost, attach instruction, BOQ gap analysis, and timely notice.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Contract is on a re-measured basis and payment is based on actual executed quantities.
rows.Beneath the Lines: Quantities can increase or decrease, but rates and risk wording still matter. More quantity is not automatically a new scope claim.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Measurement records must be timely and supported.
rows.Money Impact: Payment follows measured work, not tender BOQ quantity warranty.
rows.Schedule Impact: Quantity change may affect time only if it impacts critical path and is claimed.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Keep survey sheets, IR approvals, measurement sheets, and BOQ mapping.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Employer gives no warranty that BOQ quantities are accurate.
rows.Beneath the Lines: The Contractor cannot rely only on tender quantities to claim surprise. The claim must be tied to changed scope, instruction, or unforeseeable condition.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Claim notice still required if quantity change delays or costs more than normal remeasurement.
rows.Schedule Impact: Possible only if actual quantity change affects critical path and is properly proved.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Compare tender BOQ, IFC drawings, actual measurements, and programme impact.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Accepted amount is fixed and final, inclusive of compensation, contingencies, future law, fuel, and currency changes except specified material adjustment.
rows.Beneath the Lines: This is a strong anti-claim clause. Most market escalation arguments are blocked unless they fit the concrete/steel adjustment formula.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Use price adjustment clause only where allowed.
rows.Schedule Impact: No direct EOT from price movement.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Separate allowed concrete/steel adjustment from general inflation claims.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Concrete and steel may be adjusted using CAPMAS indices if delay is not due to Contractor.
rows.Beneath the Lines: Price adjustment is conditional. If Employer/Engineer says the Contractor caused the delay, the adjustment may be rejected.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Need proof delay was not Contractor-caused.
rows.Money Impact: Potential recovery for concrete/steel escalation only.
rows.Schedule Impact: Depends on non-contractor delay period and affected procurement.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Prepare CAPMAS index comparison, baseline prices, procurement dates, and delay responsibility analysis.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Employer/Engineer site mobilization, authority permits/licenses, relocation/protection of utilities, and dewatering are excluded.
rows.Beneath the Lines: These are possible entitlement areas, but only if actually instructed or required and not already covered elsewhere.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Variation/claim notice required before or immediately after impact.
rows.Money Impact: Potential additional payment if outside scope and instructed/required.
rows.Schedule Impact: Potential EOT if critical and not Contractor fault.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Record instruction, site condition, authority requirement, photographs, and cost/time impact.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Advance payment is 25 percent; 30 percent cash against bank check and 70 percent as steel supplied by Employer according to approved programme.
rows.Beneath the Lines: Steel supply is commercially tied to the advance. But entitlement depends on approved programme and proper requisitions.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Steel delay notices should be immediate and linked to approved programme dates.
rows.Schedule Impact: Late steel may support delay only if critical and properly requested.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Keep approved programme, steel requisitions, delivery notes, and impact analysis.
